channel.title: UN Meetings Coverage and Press Releases

item.title: Sixth Committee Concludes Work for 2026, Sending 23 Texts to General Assembly
item.description: Concluding the main part of its eighty-first session today, the Sixth Committee (Legal) approved, without a vote, 21 draft resolutions and 2 draft decisions as it upheld its tradition of consensus even though some delegations objected to the lack of progress on certain topics.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Activities of Secretary-General in Türkiye, 9-13 November
item.description: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres arrived in Antalya, Türkiye, late on Monday night, 9 November, to attend the thirty-first meeting of the Conference of the Parties of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, also known as COP31.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Commission on the Limits of Continental Shelf Concludes Sixty-Eighth Session
item.description: The Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf held its sixty-eighth session at United Nations Headquarters, from 19 October to 20 November.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Security Council ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee Amends 81 Entries on Its Sanctions List
item.description: On 20 November 2026, the entries below on the ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List of individuals and entities subject to the assets freeze, travel ban and arms embargo set out in paragraph 1 of Security Council resolution 2734 (2024) were amended following the 2025 Annual Review conducted in accordance with paragraphs 92-95 of resolution 2734 (2024).
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Security Council ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee Amends One Entry on Its Sanctions List
item.description: On 20 November 2026, the Security Council Committee pursuant to resolutions 1267 (1999), 1989 (2011) and 2253 (2015) concerning ISIL (Da’esh), Al-Qaida and associated individuals, groups, undertakings and entities enacted the amendments specified with strikethrough and underline in the entry below on its ISIL (Da’esh) and Al-Qaida Sanctions List of individuals and entities subject to the assets freeze, travel ban and arms embargo set out in paragraph 1 of Security Council resolution 2734 (2024), and adopted under Chapter VII of the Charter of the United Nations.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
item.description: Since September, more than 400 Israeli settler attacks linked to the ongoing Palestinian olive harvest have resulted in casualties or damage to property in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including to more than 4,000 trees and saplings, according to the Humanitarian Country Team.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Security Council Hears Updates on Three Subsidiary Bodies Tackling Da’esh, Al-Qaida, Terrorism Threats
item.description: The Security Council today was briefed by Sanita Pavļuta-Deslandes (Latvia), Council President for November, acting as Chair of three subsidiary bodies, which relate to Da’esh, Al-Qaida and UN counter-terrorism efforts, as well as measures to prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction to non-State actors.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Third Committee Concludes Session, Approves 11 Texts amid Divisions over Palestinian Rights, Racism, Drug Policy
item.description: The Third Committee (Social, Humanitarian and Cultural) today approved eleven draft resolutions, backing Palestinian self-determination and rejecting amendments to a global drug policy text amid sharp divisions over racism, refugee protection and international cooperation against environmental crime.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
item.description: The Secretary-General welcomed today’s judgment of the International Court of Justice in The Gambia v. Myanmar case as a powerful recognition of the Rohingya victims of genocide. He said impunity for such horrific acts must not stand and Myanmar must act in line with its obligation to comply with the Court’s decision.
item.dc:creator: United Nations
